dialect.detail: Likely AcuCOBOL or similar screen-handling COBOL (possibly Micro Focus variant) used in a French-language HR/payroll system; uses ACCEPT/DISPLAY with LINE/POSITION/SIZE clauses, CONTROL 'UPPER', TAB UPDATE NO BEEP CURSOR, and C$RERR runtime call typical of AcuCOBOL
evidence: ACCEPT ... LINE ... POSITION ... SIZE ... TAB UPDATE NO BEEP CURSOR ... CONTROL 'UPPER'

purpose.domain_detail: French-language HR/payroll system - detail of defined days for cost centers, special SOCOM module; handles employee presence, career records, cost codes, calendars
purpose.summary: Program 3-DHSOC displays and processes a detail screen of defined working days per cost center/post for a specific month in a French HR system. It reads employee registry and presence records, filters by status and cost code, and outputs formatted reports via a 215-column form handler. The program supports interactive screen navigation with function key handling.

notable_features: 42 COPY statements for modular record/file definitions
Interactive screen handling with ACCEPT LINE/POSITION/SIZE/TAB UPDATE NO BEEP CURSOR
CALL to C$RERR (AcuCOBOL runtime error routine)
LINKAGE SECTION with PROCEDURE DIVISION USING
EVALUATE used extensively for screen zone dispatch
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
verdict.notes: Source is truncated to first 16000 chars; full program is 835 lines. French comments and variable names throughout. The screen-handling syntax (TAB UPDATE NO BEEP CURSOR, CONTROL 'UPPER') is characteristic of AcuCOBOL but could also be Micro Focus. Program-ID '3-DHSOC' uses a non-standard hyphenated name starting with digit, which is allowed in some dialects. The program_type is classified as online-cics equivalent (interactive terminal) though no CICS is used - it uses native screen I/O.
